issues.quote: its note records the review and retrospective too, so its adaptation leaves the parts listed in Core concepts in place
issues.text: The note (lines 1-39) records length, goal, sprint backlog, daily, review, retrospective; it records no product backlog and no planning meeting. "leaves the parts ... in place" asserts more than the note shows.
issues.fix: Write: "and its note records the review and retrospective too, so nothing in it leaves out one of the parts listed in Core concepts."

issues.quote: the work moved instead, through the product backlog into the next sprint
issues.text: Line 17 says only "Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau" (moved to the next sprint); the route through the product backlog is the Guide's rule (claim 11: "it returns to the Product Backlog"), not something the note records.
issues.fix: Write: "the work moved to the next sprint instead; by the reference's rule it goes back to the product backlog first."

junior.reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 (junior reader simulation, prompt 05, round 2; known_vocab = 42 foundation terms, lesson vocab = [sprint], prereq = management.l1.how-software-gets-made five-line summary only)

issues.quote: it sizes each piece of work with a number, which the reference permits without naming a unit
issues.text: Earlier the `Ước lượng` numbers were 'the team's guess of how big the piece is'. Here 'without naming a unit' made me stop: I had assumed 3 meant three days. I cannot tell whether that assumption is wrong or just not the point.
issues.fix: Add one clause after 'without naming a unit' saying whether the team's numbers are days or relative sizes, or drop 'without naming a unit'.

issues.quote: the team demonstrates on a shared test environment, a machine kept for trying things out, not one person's own
issues.text: I understand what a shared test environment is, but not why demonstrating on one person's machine would be a problem. The sentence states the rule and moves on.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence saying why: e.g. what works on one developer's machine may not be what the team actually has finished.

issues.quote: two people reading the code of anything above three in that column
issues.text: 'That column' points back two paragraphs to `Ước lượng`; I had to scroll up. Also no row in the table is above three, so I wondered whether I had misread the numbers.
issues.fix: Replace 'in that column' with 'in the `Ước lượng` column', and add 'from the next sprint on' so it is clear no current piece qualifies.

issues.quote: It kept the parts that stay the same every sprint — the fixed length, one goal, the daily, the rule about what counts as finished — and its note records the review and retrospective too, so its adaptation leaves the parts listed in Core concepts in place.
issues.text: I re-read this twice: one list of kept parts, then two more, then a pointer to Core concepts. The next paragraph opens 'The ones worth arguing about' and I had to work out that 'ones' means adaptations.
issues.fix: Split the sentence in two, and start the next paragraph with 'The adaptations worth arguing about'.

issues.quote: names these six parts and a few more, and calls the roles accountabilities.
issues.text: This sentence sits between the diagram and the prose that walks it, so it interrupts the narration. 'Accountabilities' is never used again; I stopped to wonder whether I need to remember it.
issues.fix: Move the sentence to the end of the section, or drop 'and calls the roles accountabilities'.

issues.quote: Take that piece out of this sprint and back to the product backlog, and end the two weeks on the date they were fixed at.
issues.text: Option a is clearly the longest and the only one with two careful clauses; I could pick it by shape before reading the others.
issues.fix: Shorten option a (en and vi), e.g. 'Move that piece back to the product backlog and end the sprint on its date.'

issues.quote: False, because the increment is only what is finished to the standard agreed in advance, and the note moved that piece out instead.
issues.text: Option c is nearly the Core concepts wording ('finished to the standard the team agreed in advance'), so it can be matched by phrase rather than understood.
issues.fix: Paraphrase option c (en and vi), e.g. 'False, because nearly-there work does not count, and the note sent that piece to the next sprint.'
